answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a $100 bond before accepting work, whether it sells river forecasts, mirror designs, or grove surveys. Payment and bond release wait until a challenge period ends; a verifiable failure, such as a forged data signature, forfeits the bond. Creating 1,000 identities therefore ties up $100,000, and abandoning a caught identity destroys its stake rather than letting the attacker reset for free.
